transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you too. Um... I hope I'm doing this right, coming here. I just... well, it's work stuff, mostly. I drive transit, and I know they have to monitor us, obviously, that's just part of the job. But... I'm here because dispatch and compliance, they've been tracking my route changes through the computer system. And they make these little comments on the radio. People tell me it's just normal oversight, you know, just doing their jobs, and maybe I'm making too big a deal out of it... but I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it okay.
Have you been feeling unusually depressed, or perhaps abnormally energetic and talkative, during the time you've been having these concerns about work?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, you know? So I wouldn't say I've been depressed or feeling down. And I haven't been... like, overly energetic or anything either. 

I mean, I hope I'm not talking too much right now! Am I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. But no, my mood has been pretty steady, I think. I just try to go in and do a good job. Is that what you meant?
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice?

Oh! Um... no. No, definitely not. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I know that's probably just a standard question you have to ask everyone, right? 

But no, I just hear the normal things, like the dispatch radio and the passengers talking on the bus. I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm... well, you know, totally out of touch with reality or anything. I just notice the route tracking and the specific comments the other drivers make. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking.
